d: Reception room in the house of the Bojaren Grigori Gryaznoj. In the background a low entrance door, next to it a counter, full of cups, wine cups and bowls. On the right side three magnificent windows and before it a long table covered with a tablecloth; on the table candles in high silver lampstands, some salt barrels and a spice stand. On the left side a door to the inner chambers and a long bench covered with a colorfully decorated cloth. On the wall a hunting spit leans and hangs a crossbow, a large knife, various garments and ? not far from the door to the fore stage ? a bear fur. On the walls to both sides there are tables and benches, covered with red cloth. Gryaznoj stands with thoughtfully lowered head at the window
The door in the middle opens
Lyubasha sneaks through the side door. Gryaznoj comes in with a lowered head. Lyubasha quietly opens the door and goes to Gryaznoj

Chorus (the people), Oprichniki and a young boy street in the Aleksandrovsky suburb. On the front left a house (inhabited by the Sobakins) with three windows to the street and a gate in the fence; at the gate, under the window there is a wooden bench. On the right the house of Bomelius with a gate; behind it, in the background, fence and gate of a monastery. Opposite the monastery, on the left in the background, the house of Prince Gvosdev-Rostovsky with a high roofed entrance leading to the road. Autumnal landscape; in red and yellow shimmering trees. Towards evening. People come from the monastery.

Marfa does not answer and looks into the background of the stage, where at the same time two noble riders appear. The imposing appearance of the first, wrapped in a precious coat, reveals in it Ioann Vasilyevich Grosni (Ivan the Terrible); the second rider, with a broom and a dog's head on the saddle, is one of the tsar's confidants. The tsar brings his horse to a halt and watches Marfa silently and attentively; she does not recognize the tsar, but is frightened and frozen, feeling the pervasive gaze directed at her.

Reception room in the house Sobakin. On the right three red windows; on the left in the corner a tiled stove; next to it, to the front stage, the door to the hall. In the background, in the middle, another door; on the right of it a table in front of a bench; on the left, directly next to the door, a counter. Under the windows a long bench. Vasili Sobakin, Ivan Lykov and Grigori Gryaznoj sit on the bench at the table
Sobakin comes in with candles; behind him Marfa, Dunyasha, Saburova and maid of Sobakin. Lykov goes to Marfa on a sign of Gryaznoj and stands beside them; Gryaznoj gives them cups

A passage room in the Tsar's Palace. In the background, opposite the spectators, the door into the rooms of the Tsar's. Left, in the foreground, the door to the porch. Windows with gilded lattices. The room is covered with red fabric; benches with colorful patterned water jugs. Right, in the foreground, the throne of the Tsar's with brocade. Down from the ceiling of the room hangs a crystal chandelier on a gilded chain
